synopsis: The corpus cites ICCV 2025 results on both virtual-scene fidelity and synthetic-data training benefits, with evidence limited to on-road settings [f3708, f7068, f7069]. In Chapter 5, EUVS reports an average PSNR loss of 24.6% for translation-type viewpoint shifts [f3708]. In Chapter 9, Ge et al. report improved closed-loop route completion for end-to-end automated driving when synthetic data supplements real training data [f7068]. That improvement is explicitly not proof of effectiveness for mining or construction perception, leaving off-road applicability unestablished [f7069].

relations.note: Limits the finding's applicability: automated-driving gains do not establish mining or construction perception performance.
